title: Psychometric initial validation of the Concern Coherence Scale (CCS) and exploratory assessment of its sensitivity to change within the Cognitive Coherence Tool (CCT) – a validation and feasibility study in medical students in their final clinical year
summary:
The final clinical year (Praktisches Jahr, PJ) is a demanding transition period for many medical students, in which questions about their professional role and future arise. This study evaluates a new short questionnaire, the Concern Coherence Scale (CCS; German: Anliegenkohärenz-Skala, AKS), for the first time. It is intended to capture how clear, coherent and manageable participants experience a personal, career-related concern. In addition, the study explores whether the questionnaire responds to a single structured session (Cognitive Coherence Tool, CCT). The study explicitly does not test the efficacy of the session.

Medical students in their final clinical year at Hannover Medical School can take part. After a first questionnaire appointment, participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: one group receives a CCT session immediately (approx. 60–75 minutes), the other group waits for the same time and receives the session free of charge after the study. Short online surveys follow after one week and after twelve weeks.
conditions: Psychological distress, burnout risk and uncertainty in professional identity formation among medical students in their final clinical year (healthy volunteers; no disease)

interventions.name: Intervention group: one single session with the Cognitive Coherence Tool (CCT, approx. 60–75 min) directly after baseline assessment (T1). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Enrolled medical students in their final clinical year (Praktisches Jahr) at Hannover Medical School; age ≥ 18 years; sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaires; a personal concern related to their professional future as a physician that is subjectively experienced as difficult or distressing; written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Ongoing psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment; acute mental disorder (in particular severe depressive episode, psychotic disorder; PHQ-9 ≥ 20 as exclusion indicator, clinical judgement taking precedence); previous experience with PEP or CCT; simultaneous participation in another interventional study.
